styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Design, architecture and the cathedral skyline.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Suomenlinna fortress and the harbour's past.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Island ferries, parks and seaside walks.

stays.why: Central and walkable: main station, trams and the big sights are minutes away.
Quiet old streets near the cathedral and Market Square; good for first-time sightseeing.
Livelier and cheaper, with bars and cafés; a short tram or metro ride to the centre.
Bus and metro hub under one roof; handy for day trips and late arrivals.

food: Try Finnish basics: salmon soup (lohikeitto), rye bread and Karelian pasties.
Market Square (Kauppatori) stalls sell snacks and berries in season; check opening hours on the day.
Lunch is often cheaper than dinner; look for weekday lunch offers in the centre.
Cafés serve cinnamon buns (korvapuusti) and strong filter coffee; Finns drink a lot of it.
Book popular restaurants ahead on weekends; many kitchens close earlier than in bigger cities.
more_time: Take the ferry to Suomenlinna and give the fortress half a day.
Day-trip to Porvoo old town by bus; check timetables on the day.
In summer, hop a ferry to an island like Pihlajasaari for a swim and a walk.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the cathedral, design district and a Suomenlinna ferry trip; add a night for island or Porvoo time.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near -1°C, lows -6°C, snow possible. Pack warm layers.
Still deep winter, around 0°C high and -5°C low. Short days; museums are a good bet.
Slowly warming to 2°C high, but nights stay below freezing. Watch for icy pavements.
Spring arrives: highs near 7°C, lows around 0°C. Mixed sun and showers.
Milder at 14°C high; parks green up. Still bring a jacket for evenings.
Bright and pleasant: 19°C high, 12°C low. Long daylight hours.
Warmest month, 21°C high and 14°C low. Some rain days; pack a light rain layer.
Similar to July, around 20°C high. Good for ferries and island walks.
Cooling to 15°C high; autumn colours start. Bring a warm layer.
Chilly at 9°C high and 5°C low, with more rain days. Waterproof shoes help.
Dark and damp: 5°C high, 1°C low, frequent rain days. Plan indoor sights.
Winter returns: around 1°C high and -3°C low. Snow and ice possible; dress warmly.

climate_guide.summary: Northern city with cold winters and mild, bright summers. Rain falls year-round, so pack layers.

items.title: Best time: June to August
items.text: Highs around 19–21°C with long daylight. Ideal for ferries, islands and walking.

items.title: Winter is cold (Dec–Feb)
items.text: Highs near -1 to 1°C and lows down to -6°C. Snow and ice are possible; wear warm, grippy shoes.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect roughly 9–14 rain days a month. A light waterproof layer is worth packing all year.

items.title: Spring is slow
items.text: March stays near freezing; April warms to about 7°C. Bring a jacket even on sunny days.

items.title: Autumn cools fast
items.text: September around 15°C, October about 9°C. Layers and waterproof shoes help.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket and comfortable walking shoes. Add a warm hat and gloves from November to March.

transit.best: Trams and walking in the centre; one HSL ticket covers metro, buses, trains and the Suomenlinna ferry.

modes.text: Runs on the HSL ticket system; useful for east-west trips and to the main station.
Trams cover the centre well on the same HSL ticket. Buy by contactless card, HSL app or R kiosk; cash is not accepted on board.
Buses run on the HSL ticket system and reach areas trams don't. Same ticket rules apply.
Local trains are part of HSL. Airport trains need an ABC ticket; city centre travel needs AB.
The Suomenlinna ferry is included in the HSL ticket system.
Taxis wait at ranks and the airport; Bolt and Uber operate in Helsinki.
Driving is easy but parking is costly. Walking and trams cover the centre well, so a car is rarely needed.
The centre is compact and walkable. Bikes are popular in summer, with city bike stations widespread.
